# Integrating with Gradle

It is possible to generate Kotlin bindings at compile time for Kotlin Android projects. We'd like to make a gradle plugin for that, but until then you can add to your `build.gradle` the following:

```
android.libraryVariants.all { variant ->
    def t = tasks.register("generate${variant.name.capitalize()}UniFFIBindings", Exec) {
        workingDir "${project.projectDir}"
        // Runs the bindings generation, note that you must have uniffi-bindgen installed and in your PATH environment variable
        commandLine 'uniffi-bindgen', 'generate', '<PATH TO .udl FILE>', '--language', 'kotlin', '--out-dir', "${buildDir}/generated/source/uniffi/${variant.name}/java"
    }
    variant.javaCompileProvider.get().dependsOn(t)
    def sourceSet = variant.sourceSets.find { it.name == variant.name }
    sourceSet.java.srcDir new File(buildDir, "generated/source/uniffi/${variant.name}/java")
    // XXX: I've been trying to make this work but I can't, so the compiled bindings will show as "regular sources" in Android Studio.
    idea.module.generatedSourceDirs += file("${buildDir}/generated/source/uniffi/${variant.name}/java/uniffi")
}
```

The generated bindings should appear in the project sources in Android Studio.

## Using experimental unsigned types

Unsigned integers in the defined API are translated to their equivalents in the foreign language binding, e.g. `u32` becomes Kotlin's `UInt` type. See [Built-in types](../types/builtin_types.html).

However unsigned integer types are experimental in Kotlin versions prior to 1\.5. As such they require explicit annotations to suppress warnings. Uniffi is trying to add these annotations where necessary, but currently misses some places, see [PR \#977](https://github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/pull/977) for details.

To suppress all warnings for experimental unsigned types add this to your project's `build.gradle` file:

```
allprojects {
   tasks.withType(org.jetbrains.kotlin.gradle.tasks.KotlinCompile).all {
        kotlinOptions {
            freeCompilerArgs += [
                "-Xuse-experimental=kotlin.ExperimentalUnsignedTypes",
            ]
        }
    }
}
```

> ## Update

> As of [PR \#993](https://github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/pull/993), the Kotlin backend was refactored, and it became harder to support the `@ExperimentalUnsignedTypes` annotation. Uniffi's Android customers are rapidly moving toward Kotlin 1\.5, so adding this compiler arg is no longer necessary.

## JNA dependency

UniFFI relies on [JNA](https://github.com/java-native-access/jna) for the ability to call native methods. JNA 5\.12.0 or greater is required.

Set the dependency in your `build.gradle`:

```
dependencies {
    implementation "net.java.dev.jna:jna:5.12.0@aar"
}
```

## Advise on Rust \-\> Java interop

It's highly recommend to call `AttachCurrentThread` when spawning a Rust thread, and in that thread we need to call Java functions, maybe through UniFFI's foreign interface. Otherwise, [JNA](https://github.com/java-native-access/jna) has to attach and detach a Java thread into the native thread in every function call, which is a heavy operation.

```
static VM: once_cell::sync::OnceCell<jni::JavaVM> = once_cell::sync::OnceCell::new();

// need call this function in java/kotlin first
// Before Rust 1.85 use #[export_name = "Java_com_xxx_xxx"]
// Since Rust 1.85 use #[unsafe(export_name = "Java_com_xxx_xxx")]
#[unsafe(export_name = "Java_com_xxx_xxx")]
pub extern "system" fn java_init(
    env: jni::JNIEnv,
    _class: jni::objects::JClass,
    app: jni::objects::JObject,
) {
    let vm = env.get_java_vm().unwrap();
    _ = VM.set(vm);
}

// take tokio for example, and we need to call uniffi's callback in the tokio worker threads -
tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread().on_thread_start(|| {
    let vm = VM.get().expect("init java vm");
    vm.attach_current_thread_permanently().unwrap();
}).build().unwrap();
```

To call `Java_com_xxx_xxx` you need to replace `_xxx_xxx` with the right package name and the right class name from where the function will be called. For example:

In Rust:

```
// Rust (see above for before / after Rust 1.85)
#[unsafe(export_name = "Java_com_my_package_MainActivity")]
pub extern "system" fn java_init(
// ...
```

And then in Kotlin:

```
// Kotlin
package my.package

class MainActivity : ComponentActivity() {
    external fun javaInit()

    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        // Loads "libmy_library.so" so that it can be called by "external fun" above
        System.loadLibrary("my_library")
        // Calls the Java_com_my_package_MainActivity function in Rust
        javaInit()
    }
```

## Coroutines dependency

UniFFI relies on [kotlinx coroutines core](https://github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.coroutines) for future and async support. Version 1\.6 or greater is required.

Set the dependency in your `build.gradle`:

```
dependencies {
    implementation "org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-coroutines-core:1.6.4"
}
```

# Getting started

Say your company has a simple `math` crate with the following `lib.rs`:

```
fn add(a: u32, b: u32) -> u32 {
    a + b
}
```

And top brass would like you to expose this *business-critical* operation to Kotlin and Swift.  
**Don't panic!** We will show you how do that using UniFFI.

# Describing the interface

There are two ways of describing your interface:

## Proc macros

[Rust proc macros](../proc_macro/index.html) can describe your interface \- you'd define the function as:

```
#[uniffi::export]
fn add(a: u32, b: u32) -> u32 { a + b }
```

You need to [set up the scaffolding](Rust_scaffolding.html) with `uniffi::setup_scaffolding!()` \- but that's it.

## A UDL File

We describe in a UDL (a type of IDL, Interface Definition Language) file *what* is exposed and available to foreign-language bindings. In this case, we are only playing with primitive types (`u32`) and not custom data structures but we still want to expose the `add` method.

Let's create a `math.udl` file in the `math` crate's `src/` folder:

```
namespace math {
  u32 add(u32 a, u32 b);
};
```

Here you can note multiple things:

- The `namespace` directive: it will be the name of your Kotlin/Swift package. It **must** be present in any udl file, even if there aren't any exposed functions (e.g. `namespace foo {}`). It will typically be your crate name.

- The `add` function is in the `namespace` block. That's because on the Rust side it is a top-level *function*, we will see later how to to handle *methods*.

- Rust's `u32` is also UDL's `u32`, but it is not always true! See the [Built-in Types](../types/builtin_types.html) chapter for more information on mapping types between Rust and UDL.

**Note:** If any of the things you expose in the `udl` file do not have an equivalent in your Rust crate, you will get a hard error. Try changing the `u32` result type to `u64` and see what happens!

# Rust scaffolding

UniFFI requires that our generated Rust "scaffolding" code is included in your project. For proc macros, most of this is conveniently generated by the macros.

If you use UDL files, you need to generate this "scaffolding" then include the generated .rs in your project.

## Rust scaffolding code for UDL

Crates using UDL need a `build.rs` file next to `Cargo.toml`. This uses `uniffi` to generate the Rust scaffolding code.

```
fn main() {
    uniffi::generate_scaffolding("src/math.udl").unwrap();
}
```

It will generate `<namespace>.uniffi.rs` under your `target` directory.

Lastly, we include the generated scaffolding code in our `lib.rs` using this handy macro:

```
uniffi::include_scaffolding!("math");
```

## Setup for crates using only proc macros

If you are only using proc macros, you can skip `build.rs` entirely! All you need to do is add this to the top of `lib.rs`

```
uniffi::setup_scaffolding!();
```

Don't use `uniffi::setup_scaffolding!()` in a crate which uses `uniffi::include_scaffolding!()`.

If you don't specify a [`namespace`](../types/namespace.html) the crate name is used.

### Libraries that depend on UniFFI components

Suppose you want to create a shared library that includes one or more components using UniFFI. The typical way to achieve this is to create a new crate that depends on the component crates. However, this can run into issues where public symbols from the dependent crates aren't re-exported, resulting in these symbols not being available at runtime.

If you encounter this, you can use the `uniffi_reexport_scaffolding!()` macro as a work around. For example, `foo_component::uniffi_reexport_scaffolding!();` in your library's `lib.rs` will have UniFFI generate workaround code that forces `foo_component`s functions to be exported from the library.

Each scaffolding function contains a hash that's derived from the namespace. This avoids name collisions when combining multiple UniFFI components into one library.

# Foreign-language bindings

By now you have setup your crate and `cargo build` has successfully created your library.

The next step is to have UniFFI generate source code for your foreign language. It doesn't help you build this code, it just generates it for you.

## Creating the bindgen binary

First, make sure you have installed all the [prerequisites](Prerequisites.html).

Ideally you would then run the `uniffi-bindgen` binary from the `uniffi` crate to generate your bindings, but if not on [Cargo nightly](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/unstable.html#artifact-dependencies), you need to create a binary in your project that does the same thing.

While the general principles are the same, the setup differs whether you are a single crate or in a cargo workspace, but either way, you'll end up with a `cargo run [...] uniffi-bindgen ...` command to generate the bindings.

### Single crate

Add the following to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[[bin]]
# This can be whatever name makes sense for your project, but the rest of this tutorial assumes uniffi-bindgen.
name = "uniffi-bindgen"
path = "uniffi-bindgen.rs"
```

Create `uniffi-bindgen.rs`:

```
fn main() {
    uniffi::uniffi_bindgen_main()
}
```

You can now run `uniffi-bindgen` from your project using `cargo run --features=uniffi/cli --bin uniffi-bindgen [args]`

### Multi-crate workspaces

In a multiple crates workspace, you can create a separate crate for running `uniffi-bindgen`:

- Name the crate `uniffi-bindgen`, add it to your workspace.

- Add this dependency to `Cargo.toml`: `uniffi = {version = "0.XX.0", features = ["cli"] }`

- As above, add the `uniffi-bindgen` binary target

Then you can run `uniffi-bindgen` from any crate in your project using `cargo run -p uniffi-bindgen [args]`

## Running uniffi-bindgen using a library file

Use `generate --library` to generate foreign bindings by using a cdylib file built for your library. This can be more convenient than specifying the UDL file \-- especially when multiple UniFFI-ed crates are built together in one library. This should be used where possible \- some "external type" features don't work otherwise.

In our example, we generate the bindings with:

```
cargo build --release
cargo run --bin uniffi-bindgen generate --library target/release/libmath.so --language kotlin --out-dir out
```

(probably `.dylib` on mac, good luck with `.dll`!)

Then look in the `out` directory.

When using library mode, if multiple crates get built into the library that use UniFFI, all will have bindings generated for them.

Library mode comes with some extra requirements:

- It must be run from within the cargo workspace of your project

- Each crate must use exactly 1 UDL file when compiling the Rust library. However, crates can have multiple UDL files as long as they ensure only one is used for any particular build, e.g. by using feature flags.

- Rust sources must use `uniffi::include_scaffolding!` to include the scaffolding code.

### Cross platform and multi architecture support

UniFFI metadata embedded in libraries is platform and architecture agnostic, which might be useful in cross-compiled environments. You must still take care here, as the underlying Rust code could have its own conditional compilation; only the exact library is guaranteed to have the correct metadata for that library.

## Running uniffi-bindgen with a single UDL file

Generating from a single UDL is deprecated \- a single crate with no proc-macro implementations doesn't seem realistic \- but we support it aalmost by accident for legacy reasons.

Use the `generate` command to generate bindings by specifying a UDL file.

### Kotlin

From the example directory, run:

```
cargo run --bin uniffi-bindgen generate src/math.udl --language kotlin
```

then have a look at `src/uniffi/math/math.kt`

### Swift

Run

```
cargo run --bin uniffi-bindgen generate src/math.udl --language swift
```

then check out `src/math.swift`

### Ruby

Run

```
cargo run --bin uniffi-bindgen generate src/math.udl --language ruby
```

then check out `src/math.rb`

Note that these commands could be integrated as part of your gradle/Xcode build process.

This is it, you have an MVP integration of UniFFI in your project.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Audit and finish the Kotlin-to-Rust migration in Watermelon MediaPlayer.
- Current request: after approving all proposals, complete Stages 3–6 (Rust port, binding, parity, cutover, cleanup) with all execution through GitHub Actions.

## Requirements
- No local tests, no local toolchain installation; all builds/tests via GitHub Actions workflows.
- Local checks only: YAML parse, `git diff --check`, `sha256sum -c`.
- Keep unrelated pre-existing `Docs/` → `docs/` changes excluded from all commits.
- Owner decisions must be explicit; proposals are not approvals unless the owner says so.
- User wording: “Approve all proposals (Recommended)” and “finish the migration”.

## Decisions
- Owner approved D-1–D-6 on `2026-11-23`, recorded in `docs/migration/decision-log.md`.
- D-1: Continue past G0, conditional on G0 being met first.
- D-2: UniFFI with a time-boxed spike; measure `SpeechLikelihoodAccumulator` ByteBuffer copy cost before committing to all twelve ports.
- D-3: 1e-6 tolerance for derived floats; bit-exact integer/Long/hash outputs; raw IEEE-754 bits diagnostic only.
- D-4: Local-only opt-in debug logging of Kotlin vs Rust outputs; no telemetry/upload.
- D-5: Keep pure-Java MP3 encoder in `media-tools`.
- D-6: Approve one implementation owner + one independent reviewer before Stage 3 review; names still not supplied.

## Work State
### Completed
- Audit report and post-audit action table created in `docs/migration/migration-process-audit.md`.
- Golden oracle scaffolding, generators, self-checks and workflows added; Bidi and OSHash Kotlin defects fixed before freezing oracle.
- Branch `migration/golden-oracle-scaffolding` pushed via SSH with 8 migration-only commits: `292f80e`, `a4dd974`, `bf9af08`, `b65ce67`, `0bbe6c4`, `76981c0`, `06715c1`, `ac7275a`.
- Oracle run `45074382455` passed: 10 JSON files, 39 cases, 111,890 bytes, byte-identical two runs, both self-checks; corpus committed under `testdata/golden/` with `SHA256SUMS`.
- `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` passes locally as a static check.
- First oracle run `45074069540` failed due Gradle `UP-TO-DATE`; fixed by adding `--rerun` to all generator/self-check/benchmark invocations.
- Full CI green on `06715c1`: `45075903852` (5/5 jobs). Earlier green full CI: `45074866004`.
- Benchmark run `45075503837` passed: 7 workloads × 20 raw nanosecond samples; raw data in `docs/migration/benchmark-results/`.
- `PLAN.md`, `g0-report.md`, `stage-2-report.md`, `baseline-benchmarks.md`, audit table, `proposed-decisions.md` and `decision-log.md` reconciled with dated post-approval records.
- Temporary branch `push` triggers removed; both migration workflows are `workflow_dispatch`-only.
- PR #73 opened (`migration/golden-oracle-scaffolding` → `main`), title `Stage 2 evidence: fix Kotlin defects, freeze golden oracle, record JVM baseline`; factual tracking comment added to merged PR #72.
- PR #73 checks restarted on new head `ac7275a` after the decision commit; no final PR check result captured yet.
- Explore agent completed mapping of all 12 Kotlin candidates, module/build setup, golden schema, CI patterns, composition root, `verify_interfaces.py` and Stage 3–6 deliverables.
- Rust workspace scaffolding created: `rust/Cargo.toml`, `rust/crates/core/Cargo.toml`, and modules `contracts.rs`, `bidi.rs`, `srt.rs`, `hash.rs`, `time_mapper.rs`, `drift.rs`, `correlator.rs`, `consensus.rs`, `json_util.rs`, `probe.rs`, `activity.rs`, `speech.rs`, `lib.rs`.

### Active
- Writing `rust/crates/core/src/bin/parity.rs` to load `testdata/golden/*.json`, dispatch all 10 components and compare outputs using D-3.
- Adding a Rust/NDK/UniFFI CI workflow and running Rust compile/parity in GitHub Actions.
- Time-boxed UniFFI spike, including PCM copy-cost measurement at the `SpeechLikelihoodAccumulator` `ByteBuffer` boundary.
- Stage 4 shadow-mode flag in `AppDependencies.kt`, local-only Kotlin-vs-Rust debug logging, cutover/rollback flag, Stage 6 cleanup and `verify_interfaces.py` updates.
- Updating `PLAN.md` and stage reports with Stage 3–6 progress only after CI evidence exists.

### Blocked
- D-6 names: implementation owner and independent reviewer not supplied; Stage 3 review cannot be signed off.
- Golden-vector JSON schema in `PLAN.md` still not explicitly confirmed by owner.
- Official `breakdance.avi` OSHash media not supplied; no copyrighted media committed.
- On-device ART protocol and acceptance threshold undefined; only JVM microbenchmark evidence exists.
- Rust CI has not run yet; `parity.rs` and the Rust workflow are not yet written/committed.
- PR #73 checks on `ac7275a` were pending/in progress at last check.

## Next Move
1. Finish `rust/crates/core/src/bin/parity.rs` with exact golden input structs, D-3 comparison, per-case PASS/FAIL output and non-zero exit on mismatch.
2. Add `.github/workflows/migration-rust-parity.yml` with pinned actions, Rust toolchain setup, `cargo test`, `cargo run ... -- --golden-dir testdata/golden`, and artifacts.
3. Commit only migration paths (`rust/**`, workflow, migration docs) with `git diff --check`; exclude unrelated `Docs/` changes.
4. Run the Rust workflow via `gh workflow run`, inspect CI logs, fix compile/parity failures through GitHub Actions only.
5. Add UniFFI spike scaffolding and PCM copy-cost benchmark; run in CI before expanding binding usage.
6. Add Stage 4 shadow/cutover flags in `app/src/main/kotlin/com/watermelon/app/AppDependencies.kt`, local-only logging, and rollback criteria.
7. Complete Stage 5–6 ports/cleanup, update `verify_interfaces.py`, then update stage reports/PR #73 honestly; do not claim G1–G3 or full completion until CI and owner-supplied items are satisfied.

- `docs/migration/decision-log.md`: authoritative D-1–D-6 approvals dated `2026-11-23`.
- `docs/migration/proposed-decisions.md`: rationale for approved proposals and remaining owner inputs.
- `docs/migration/PLAN.md`: stage/gate matrix, reconstructed oracle contract, needs Stage 3–6 updates.
- `docs/migration/kotlin-signatures.md`: inventory of the 12 migration candidates.
- `docs/migration/migration-process-audit.md`: audit findings and post-audit action table.
- `testdata/golden/`: verified Kotlin oracle corpus, `SHA256SUMS`, README.
- `rust/Cargo.toml`: new Rust workspace root.
- `rust/crates/core/src/lib.rs`: module exports; parity binary still to be added under `src/bin/`.
- `rust/crates/core/src/contracts.rs`: serde models and golden float wrappers.
- `rust/crates/core/src/speech.rs`: PCM accumulator port and golden PCM synthesizer.
- `subtitle-engine/src/test/kotlin/com/watermelon/subtitle/golden/SubtitleGoldenVectorGeneratorTest.kt`: generator/schema for 9 vectors.
- `media-tools/src/test/kotlin/com/watermelon/mediatools/subtitle/sync/SpeechAccumulatorGoldenVectorGeneratorTest.kt`: 10th vector generator.
- `.github/workflows/migration-golden-vectors.yml`: oracle generation/checksum pattern.
- `.github/workflows/migration-baseline-benchmarks.yml`: benchmark pattern and metadata capture.
- `app/src/main/kotlin/com/watermelon/app/AppDependencies.kt`: composition root seam for shadow/cutover flags.

## Important Context
- Oracle schema: `{component, generator, cases:[{id,input,output}]}`; 10 files, 39 cases, 111,890 bytes.
- Components: `srt_parse`, `bidi_format`, `hash_opensubtitles`, `time_mapper`, `drift_corrector`, `correlator`, `consensus`, `probe_select`, `activity_builder`, `speech_accumulator`.
- Floats are objects `{"decimal":"...","bits":"..."}`; f32 bits 8 hex chars, f64 bits 16 hex chars.
- `activity_builder` output is a bare signature; `drift_corrector` has two case shapes; `speech_accumulator` vectors omit PCM bytes and must synthesize the deterministic 8 s / 16 kHz / mono signal.
- D-3 comparison: float decimal tolerance 1e-6, exact integers/Long/hash strings, bits diagnostic only.
- Kotlin `Double.roundToLong()` is `floor(x + 0.5)`, implemented as `kotlin_round_to_long` in Rust.
- Gradle commands must use `--rerun`; `UP-TO-DATE` previously invalidated oracle evidence.
- OAuth token lacks `workflow` scope; pushes used `git push git@github.com:SMozaff/Watermelon-MediaPlayer.git migration/golden-oracle-scaffolding`.
- `gh workflow run migration-golden-vectors.yml --ref ...` returned HTTP 404 before the workflow existed on the default branch; temporary `push` triggers were removed afterward.
- Benchmark host metadata: `ubuntu-latest` image `20261116.202.1`, Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, kernel `Linux 7.0.0-1020-azure`, AMD EPYC 7763 4 vCPU, Temurin/OpenJDK 17.0.21, Gradle 9.7.1, captured `2026-11-22T22:03:47Z`.
- Unrelated working-tree changes remain unstaged: deleted `Docs/...` files and untracked `docs/DOSSIER.md`, `docs/ICON_SYSTEM.md`, `docs/Subtitle_System_Blueprint.docx`, `docs/UI_MANIFEST.md`, `docs/WatermelonPlayer UI.png`.

# Kotlin-to-Rust migration plan (working definition)

**Status:** Working document. The migration brief that defined "six stages" was not committed to
this repository; the stage and gate names below are reconstructed from the stage reports. The owner
approved the D-1…D-6 proposals on 2026-11-23, which authorizes Stage 3 onward; the reconstructed
schema in this file is still awaiting explicit confirmation.

This file is the single place to check stage order, exit criteria and decision owners. Individual
reports remain the evidence of what actually ran.

## Stage and gate matrix

| Stage | Purpose | Exit criteria | Gate / decision | Current state |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — Hygiene, discovery, baseline harness | Remove stale outputs; inventory the twelve candidates; add opt-in JVM benchmarks | Signature inventory complete; harness compiles; build/tests green in CI | None (entry) | **Done.** PR #71 merged, CI green. JVM baselines recorded in CI run `45075503837` on a named `ubuntu-latest` runner; no ART/device baseline. |
| 2 — Golden vectors and test-gap closure | Generate the Kotlin behavior oracle; close direct-test gaps | Generator + 10 JSON files + Kotlin self-check + two-run checksum proof; corpus < 5 MB; target tests pass | **G0 / D-1** continue or stop | **Gate passed.** PR #72 merged as PARTIAL; the post-audit branch closed the generator, 39 cases in 10 files, self-check and byte-identical two-run proof (CI run `45074382455`), and full CI is green (`45075903852`). D-1 approved 2026-11-23; owner schema confirmation and official OSHash media vector remain open. |
| 3 — Rust core + binding spike | Decide binding tool and tolerance; port one component end-to-end; measure FFI/copy cost | D-2 and D-3 approved; one function runs on device with bit/decimal comparison; NDK toolchain in CI | **G1** (proposed) | Not started. No Rust/Cargo/NDK files. |
| 4 — Remaining ports + shadow mode | Port remaining candidates behind approved seams; run Kotlin and Rust side by side locally | All ten vectors pass against Rust; D-4 logging policy approved; no user-visible behavior change | **G2** (proposed) | Not started. |
| 5 — Cutover | Switch runtime calls to Rust behind a flag; validate on device | Device parity on representative media; rollback criteria met; D-5/D-6 approved | **G3** (proposed) | Not started. |
| 6 — Cleanup | Remove superseded Kotlin implementations and migration scaffolding | No orphaned interfaces; `verify_interfaces.py` updated; docs archived | Done criteria (proposed) | Not started. |

## Rules that apply at every stage

1. `docs/migration/decision-log.md` accepts **owner decisions only**. A blank cell is not a choice
   and must not be inferred from a proposal, a report, or code.
2. A stage is complete only when its own acceptance table is complete. A merged PR is not proof
   of stage completion; check the report and the artifacts it names.
3. Production behavior changes are separate, explicitly approved tasks. The oracle is generated
   from the code as it exists at generation time, so behavior fixes must land **before** the
   vectors are frozen.
4. All execution evidence comes from CI or a named checkout. Reports must state the session,
   date and exact command; "it cannot be done" is never a valid substitute for a run attempt.

## Decision ownership

| Decision | Owner | Required by | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-1 Continue past G0 | Repository owner | Start of Stage 3 | Approved 2026-11-23 (continue) |
| D-2 Binding tool | Repository owner | Stage 3 spike | Approved 2026-11-23 (UniFFI + spike) |
| D-3 Float tolerance | Repository owner | Stage 3 spike | Approved 2026-11-23 (1e-6 floats, exact ints/hashes) |
| D-4 Shadow-mode logging | Repository owner | Stage 4 | Approved 2026-11-23 (local only) |
| D-5 MP3 encoder | Repository owner | Stage 5 | Approved 2026-11-23 (keep pure-Java encoder) |
| D-6 Migration owner and reviewer | Repository owner | Before Stage 3 | Approved 2026-11-23; names still to be supplied |

The rationale for each decision is in [proposed-decisions.md](proposed-decisions.md). The
authoritative record is [decision-log.md](decision-log.md).

## Oracle contract (to be confirmed)

Ten component files under `testdata/golden/`:

`srt_parse.json`, `bidi_format.json`, `hash_opensubtitles.json`, `time_mapper.json`,
`drift_corrector.json`, `correlator.json`, `consensus.json`, `probe_select.json`,
`activity_builder.json`, `speech_accumulator.json`.

Generation is implemented by the generator tests in `subtitle-engine` and `media-tools` and is
driven by `.github/workflows/migration-golden-vectors.yml` (`workflow_dispatch`). The workflow
proves two runs are byte-identical, checks the 10-file corpus is under 5 MB, runs the structural
self-check, and uploads the corpus as an artifact. Run `45074382455` passed all of these and the
verified corpus is committed under `testdata/golden/` with `SHA256SUMS` and provenance notes. The
workflow does not write to the repository; regenerate and recommit when behavior changes.

Each file contains a deterministic, sorted list of cases. Every floating-point result is
recorded twice: as a decimal string and as raw IEEE-754 bits (`f32`/`f64`) so that a tolerance
decision (D-3) can be applied later without regenerating the corpus. Generation is executed by
`workflow_dispatch` in GitHub Actions and must be byte-identical across two consecutive runs.

# Proposed decisions for owner approval

**Status:** Approved by the repository owner on 2026-11-23. D-1 through D-6 are now recorded in
`docs/migration/decision-log.md`, which remains the only authoritative decision record. This file
is retained as the rationale for those decisions, not as a second decision log.

Prepared 2026-11-23 from [migration-process-audit.md](migration-process-audit.md).

## D-1 — Continue past G0?

**Proposal:** Continue, conditional on G0 actually being met first.

**Rationale:** G0 currently has no golden corpus and no benchmark measurements, so "continue"
cannot be evaluated on evidence. The recommendation is to continue only after the generator,
ten JSON files, self-check, two-run checksum proof and at least one recorded benchmark run exist.
A stop decision remains legitimate if the measured JVM/device difference does not justify the
FFI and maintenance cost.

**Consequence if accepted:** Stage 3 may start only after the G0 exit criteria in [PLAN.md](PLAN.md).

## D-2 — Binding tool

**Proposal:** UniFFI, with a time-boxed spike before committing to all twelve ports.

**Rationale:** UniFFI generates both sides of the boundary and keeps the type contract in one
place, which matters for the many `FloatArray` and sealed-result types in the sync contracts.
Hand-written JNI gives more control over PCM buffer copying but is easier to get subtly wrong.
The spike must measure both correctness and the copy cost at the `SpeechLikelihoodAccumulator`
`ByteBuffer` boundary; if that cost dominates, revisit this choice.

**Consequence if accepted:** Add Rust toolchain and UniFFI generation to CI in Stage 3; no JNI
code until the spike reports.

## D-3 — Float tolerance

**Proposal:** 1e-6 tolerance for derived floating-point values, bit-exact comparison for integer,
Long and hash outputs.

**Rationale:** Kotlin/JVM and Rust/libm can differ in the last bits of `ln`, `roundToLong` and
other math used by `SubtitleProbeSelectorImpl` and `OffsetConsensus`. Raw IEEE-754 bits are
recorded in every golden vector, so a stricter rule can be adopted later without regenerating
anything. Bit-exactness across JVM and Rust for transcendental functions is not a realistic
acceptance rule on Android devices.

**Consequence if accepted:** Parity checker applies 1e-6 to decimal float results and exact
equality to bits of integer/hash results; raw bits remain diagnostic evidence, not pass/fail.

## D-4 — Shadow-mode logging policy

**Proposal:** Local only — opt-in debug logging of Kotlin vs Rust outputs, no telemetry, no upload.

**Rationale:** The app is commercial and its network surface is deliberately limited to subtitle
lookups. A shadow mode is needed for safe cutover, but it must not create a new data path.

**Consequence if accepted:** Add a debug-only flag in the app composition root and document a
rollback trigger before the first port.

## D-5 — MP3 encoder

**Proposal:** Keep the pure-Java encoder in `media-tools`.

**Rationale:** It is already validated in CI and has no NDK/JNI dependency. It is not one of the
twelve port candidates, and moving it would add risk without addressing the migration goal.

## D-6 — Migration owner and reviewer

**Proposal:** Owner to name one implementation owner and one independent reviewer before Stage 3.

**Rationale:** The audit found a PARTIAL stage merged with no recorded review. A named reviewer
is the simplest control for the decision-heavy stages ahead.

187: The method calls `currentCoroutineContext().ensureActive()` at entry and again at the beginning of each candidate-loop iteration. # Rust scaffolding

UniFFI requires that our generated Rust "scaffolding" code is included in your project. For proc macros, most of this is conveniently generated by the macros.

If you use UDL files, you need to generate this "scaffolding" then include the generated .rs in your project.

## Rust scaffolding code for UDL

Crates using UDL need a `build.rs` file next to `Cargo.toml`. This uses `uniffi` to generate the Rust scaffolding code.

```rust
fn main() {
    uniffi::generate_scaffolding("src/math.udl").unwrap();
}
```

It will generate `<namespace>.uniffi.rs` under your `target` directory.

Lastly, we include the generated scaffolding code in our `lib.rs` using this handy macro:

```rust
uniffi::include_scaffolding!("math");
```

## Setup for crates using only proc macros

If you are only using proc macros, you can skip `build.rs` entirely!
All you need to do is add this to the top of `lib.rs`

```rust
uniffi::setup_scaffolding!();
```

Don't use `uniffi::setup_scaffolding!()` in a crate which uses `uniffi::include_scaffolding!()`.

If you don't specify a [`namespace`](../types/namespace.md) the crate name is used.

### Libraries that depend on UniFFI components

Suppose you want to create a shared library that includes one or more
components using UniFFI. The typical way to achieve this is to create a new
crate that depends on the component crates.  However, this can run into issues
where public symbols from the dependent crates aren't re-exported, resulting
in these symbols not being available at runtime.

If you encounter this, you can use the `uniffi_reexport_scaffolding!()` macro as a work around.
For example, `foo_component::uniffi_reexport_scaffolding!();` in your library's `lib.rs` will have
UniFFI generate workaround code that forces `foo_component`s functions to be exported from the library.

Each scaffolding function contains a hash that's derived from the namespace.
This avoids name collisions when combining multiple UniFFI components into
one library.

# Describing the interface

There are two ways of describing your interface:

## Proc macros

[Rust proc macros](../proc_macro/index.md) can describe your interface - you'd define the function as:

```
#[uniffi::export]
fn add(a: u32, b: u32) -> u32 { a + b }
```

You need to [set up the scaffolding](./Rust_scaffolding.md) with `uniffi::setup_scaffolding!()` - but that's it.

## A UDL File

We describe in a UDL (a type of IDL, Interface Definition Language) file _what_ is exposed and available to foreign-language bindings. In this case, we are only playing with primitive types (`u32`) and not custom data structures but we still want to expose the `add` method.

Let's create a `math.udl` file in the `math` crate's `src/` folder:

```idl
namespace math {
  u32 add(u32 a, u32 b);
};
```

Here you can note multiple things:

- The `namespace` directive: it will be the name of your Kotlin/Swift package. It **must** be present in any udl file, even if there aren't any exposed functions (e.g. `namespace foo {}`).
It will typically be your crate name.
- The `add` function is in the `namespace` block. That's because on the Rust side it is a top-level _function_, we will see later how to to handle _methods_.
- Rust's `u32` is also UDL's `u32`, but it is not always true! See the [Built-in Types](../types/builtin_types.md) chapter for more information on mapping types between Rust and UDL.

**Note:** If any of the things you expose in the `udl` file do not have an equivalent in your Rust crate, you will get a hard error. Try changing the `u32` result type to `u64` and see what happens!

# Foreign-language bindings

By now you have setup your crate and `cargo build` has successfully created your library.

The next step is to have UniFFI generate source code for your foreign language. It doesn't help you build this code, it just generates it for you.

## Creating the bindgen binary

First, make sure you have installed all the [prerequisites](./Prerequisites.md).

Ideally you would then run the `uniffi-bindgen` binary from the `uniffi` crate to generate your bindings,
but if not on [Cargo nightly](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/unstable.html#artifact-dependencies),
you need to create a binary in your project that does the same thing.

While the general principles are the same, the setup differs whether you are a single crate or in a cargo workspace,
but either way, you'll end up with a `cargo run [...] uniffi-bindgen ...` command to generate the bindings.

### Single crate

Add the following to your `Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[[bin]]
# This can be whatever name makes sense for your project, but the rest of this tutorial assumes uniffi-bindgen.
name = "uniffi-bindgen"
path = "uniffi-bindgen.rs"
```

Create `uniffi-bindgen.rs`:
```rust
fn main() {
    uniffi::uniffi_bindgen_main()
}
```

You can now run `uniffi-bindgen` from your project using `cargo run --features=uniffi/cli --bin uniffi-bindgen [args]`

### Multi-crate workspaces

In a multiple crates workspace, you can create a separate crate for running `uniffi-bindgen`:

  - Name the crate `uniffi-bindgen`, add it to your workspace.
  - Add this dependency to `Cargo.toml`: `uniffi = {version = "0.XX.0", features = ["cli"] }`
  - As above, add the `uniffi-bindgen` binary target

Then you can run `uniffi-bindgen` from any crate in your project using `cargo run -p uniffi-bindgen [args]`

## Running uniffi-bindgen using a library file

Pass a library path directly to `generate` to generate foreign bindings from a compiled library.
Specifying a library instead of a UDL file is convenient when multiple UniFFI'd crates are built together in one library.
UniFFI auto-detects whether the source is a library or a UDL file by its extension.

In our example, we generate the bindings with:
```
cargo build --release
cargo run --bin uniffi-bindgen generate target/release/libmath.so --language kotlin --out-dir out
```
(probably `.dylib` on mac, good luck with `.dll`!)

Then look in the `out` directory - there will be one or more generated files.

Passing a library comes with some extra requirements:

  - It must be run from within the cargo workspace of your project
  - Each crate must use exactly 1 UDL file when compiling the Rust library.  However, crates can have
    multiple UDL files as long as they ensure only one is used for any particular build,
    e.g. by using feature flags.
  - Rust sources must use `uniffi::include_scaffolding!` to include the scaffolding code.

### Cross platform and multi architecture support

UniFFI metadata embedded in libraries is platform and architecture agnostic, which might be useful in cross-compiled environments.
You must still take care here, as the underlying Rust code could have its own conditional compilation;
only the exact library is guaranteed to have the correct metadata for that library.

## Running uniffi-bindgen with a single UDL file

Generating from a single UDL is deprecated - a single crate with no proc-macro implementations doesn't seem realistic - but we support it aalmost by accident for legacy reasons.

Use the `generate` command to generate bindings by specifying a UDL file.

### Kotlin

From the example directory, run:
```
cargo run --bin uniffi-bindgen generate src/math.udl --language kotlin
```
then have a look at `src/uniffi/math/math.kt`

### Swift

Run
```
cargo run --bin uniffi-bindgen generate src/math.udl --language swift
```
then check out `src/math.swift`

### Ruby

Run
```
cargo run --bin uniffi-bindgen generate src/math.udl --language ruby
```
then check out `src/math.rb`

Note that these commands could be integrated as part of your gradle/Xcode build process.

name: Migration UniFFI spike

# D-2 time-boxed spike. Runs entirely on ubuntu-latest: compiles the Rust core and
# UniFFI boundary, measures the PCM byte-buffer copy cost, and generates Kotlin
# bindings from the compiled library. No local Rust/NDK toolchain is required.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  spike:
    name: Generate UniFFI bindings and measure PCM copy cost
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Set up Rust stable
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@df2a88e9fe4098bad09cb42c3dec7187f15861fc # stable
        with:
          toolchain: stable

      - name: Generate lockfile
        working-directory: rust
        run: cargo generate-lockfile

      - name: Compile Rust core, FFI spike and bindgen
        working-directory: rust
        run: |
          set +e
          cargo test --workspace --all-targets --locked > compile.log 2>&1
          status=$?
          set -e
          cat compile.log
          echo "cargo_exit=$status" >> compile.log
          exit $status

      - name: Build UniFFI shared library
        working-directory: rust
        run: cargo build -p watermelon-ffi --locked

      - name: Record spike host metadata
        run: |
          mkdir -p migration-uniffi
          {
            echo "captured_at_utc=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
            echo "git_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            echo "workflow_run=${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"
            echo "runner_os=$RUNNER_OS"
            echo "runner_arch=$RUNNER_ARCH"
            echo "runner_image=${ImageVersion:-unknown}"
            echo "kernel=$(uname -sr)"
            echo "os=$(. /etc/os-release && echo "$PRETTY_NAME")"
            echo "cpu_model=$(grep -m1 'model name' /proc/cpuinfo | cut -d: -f2- | xargs)"
            echo "cpu_count=$(nproc)"
            echo "rust_version=$(rustc --version)"
          } > migration-uniffi/metadata.txt
          cat migration-uniffi/metadata.txt

      - name: Measure PCM byte-buffer copy cost
        working-directory: rust
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          cargo run -p watermelon-core --bin pcm_copy_benchmark --locked -- \
            --sample-count=128000 --samples=20 | tee ../migration-uniffi/pcm-copy-report.txt

      - name: Validate raw nanosecond samples
        run: |
          pattern='BENCH name=[^[:space:]]+ warmup=[0-9]+ timed=[0-9]+ raw_ns=[0-9,]+ median_ns=[0-9]+ mean_ns=[0-9]+ checksum=-?[0-9]+'
          grep -hoE "$pattern" migration-uniffi/pcm-copy-report.txt > migration-uniffi/raw-samples.txt
          cat migration-uniffi/raw-samples.txt
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import re
          lines = [line.strip() for line in open('migration-uniffi/raw-samples.txt') if line.strip()]
          assert len(lines) == 2, f'expected 2 copy-cost workloads, found {len(lines)}'
          names = set()
          for line in lines:
              name = re.search(r'name=(\S+)', line)
              raw = re.search(r'raw_ns=([\d,]+)', line)
              assert name and raw, line
              assert name.group(1) not in names, f'duplicate workload: {name.group(1)}'
              names.add(name.group(1))
              samples = raw.group(1).split(',')
              assert len(samples) == 20 and all(sample.isdigit() for sample in samples), line
          print(f'validated {len(lines)} workloads, 20 raw samples each')
          PY

      - name: Generate Kotlin bindings from compiled library
        working-directory: rust
        run: |
          mkdir -p ../build/uniffi-kotlin
          cargo run -p uniffi-bindgen --locked -- \
            generate target/debug/libwatermelon_ffi.so \
            --language kotlin \
            --out-dir ../build/uniffi-kotlin
          find ../build/uniffi-kotlin -type f -name '*.kt' -print
          test -n "$(find ../build/uniffi-kotlin -type f -name '*.kt' -print -quit)"

      - name: Publish PCM copy-cost medians to job summary
        run: |
          echo '## PCM copy-cost spike (ns)' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo 'Host microbenchmark on ubuntu-latest; not ART/device numbers.' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          sed -n 's/^\(BENCH name=[^ ]*\).*median_ns=\([0-9]*\).*$/\1 \2/p' \
            migration-uniffi/raw-samples.txt >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Upload spike artifacts
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: migration-uniffi-spike
          path: |
            migration-uniffi/
            build/uniffi-kotlin/
            rust/compile.log
          if-no-files-found: warn

package com.watermelon.common.subtitle.sync

import com.watermelon.common.model.ParsedSubtitle

/** Compact timing signal shared by subtitle and audio analysis. Values are normalized 0f..1f. */
data class ActivitySignature(
    val startMs: Long,
    val bucketMs: Int,
    val occupancy: FloatArray,
    val onsets: FloatArray,
) {
    init {
        require(bucketMs > 0) { "bucketMs must be > 0" }
        require(occupancy.size == onsets.size) { "occupancy/onsets size mismatch" }
    }

    val durationMs: Long get() = occupancy.size.toLong() * bucketMs
}

sealed interface SubtitleSyncModel {
    data object Identity : SubtitleSyncModel
    data class Offset(val offsetMs: Long) : SubtitleSyncModel
    data class Affine(val scale: Double, val offsetMs: Long) : SubtitleSyncModel
    data class Piecewise(val anchors: List<SyncAnchor>) : SubtitleSyncModel
}

data class SyncAnchor(val subtitleTimeMs: Long, val mediaTimeMs: Long)

data class SubtitleSyncRequest(
    val mediaId: String,
    val mediaUri: String,
    val mediaFileSize: Long,
    val mediaDurationMs: Long,
    val subtitleFingerprint: String,
    val subtitleLanguage: String?,
    val subtitle: ParsedSubtitle,
    val playbackSessionId: Long,
)

data class SyncMeasurement(
    val subtitleProbeStartMs: Long,
    val audioProbeStartMs: Long,
    val estimatedOffsetMs: Long,
    val correlationScore: Float,
    val peakMargin: Float,
    val speechCoverage: Float,
    val transitionCount: Int,
    val probeQuality: Float,
)

sealed interface SubtitleSyncResult {
    data class Synchronized(
        val model: SubtitleSyncModel,
        val confidence: Float,
        val measurements: List<SyncMeasurement>,
    ) : SubtitleSyncResult

    data class ComplexDriftDetected(
        val measurements: List<SyncMeasurement>,
    ) : SubtitleSyncResult

    data class LowConfidence(
        val measurements: List<SyncMeasurement>,
    ) : SubtitleSyncResult

    data object Unsupported : SubtitleSyncResult
    data object ResourceDenied : SubtitleSyncResult
    data object Cancelled : SubtitleSyncResult
    data class Failed(val reason: String) : SubtitleSyncResult
}

enum class SyncSource { AUTO, MANUAL }

enum class SyncStatus {
    IDLE,
    CHECKING_CACHE,
    ANALYZING,
    SYNCHRONIZED,
    LOW_CONFIDENCE,
    COMPLEX_DRIFT,
    UNSUPPORTED,
    RESOURCE_DENIED,
    FAILED,
}

data class SubtitleSyncProfile(
    val mediaId: String,
    val mediaFileSize: Long,
    val subtitleFingerprint: String,
    val subtitleLanguage: String? = null,
    val autoModel: SubtitleSyncModel? = null,
    val autoConfidence: Float? = null,
    val autoEngineVersion: Int? = null,
    val autoUpdatedAt: Long? = null,
    val manualOffsetMs: Long? = null,
    val manualUpdatedAt: Long? = null,
) {
    fun effectiveModel(): SubtitleSyncModel =
        manualOffsetMs?.let(SubtitleSyncModel::Offset)
            ?: autoModel
            ?: SubtitleSyncModel.Identity

    fun effectiveOffsetMs(): Long = when (val model = effectiveModel()) {
        SubtitleSyncModel.Identity -> 0L
        is SubtitleSyncModel.Offset -> model.offsetMs
        is SubtitleSyncModel.Affine -> model.offsetMs
        is SubtitleSyncModel.Piecewise -> 0L
    }
}

data class ProbeCandidate(
    /** Source-subtitle timeline position. Audio is requested at this time + provisional offset. */
    val subtitleStartMs: Long,
    val durationMs: Long,
    val distinctiveness: Float,
)

data class CorrelationConfig(
    val minOffsetMs: Long,
    val maxOffsetMs: Long,
    val stepMs: Long,
    val onsetWeight: Float = 0.60f,
    val occupancyWeight: Float = 0.35f,
    val silenceWeight: Float = 0.05f,
    val independentPeakDistanceMs: Long = 1_000L,
)

data class CorrelationResult(
    val offsetMs: Long,
    val peakScore: Float,
    val secondPeakScore: Float,
    val peakMargin: Float,
)

interface SubtitleActivityBuilder {
    fun build(
        subtitle: ParsedSubtitle,
        startMs: Long,
        endMs: Long,
        bucketMs: Int,
    ): ActivitySignature
}

interface SubtitleProbeSelector {
    fun select(
        subtitle: ParsedSubtitle,
        mediaDurationMs: Long,
        maxCount: Int,
    ): List<ProbeCandidate>
}

interface ActivityCorrelator {
    fun correlate(
        audio: ActivitySignature,
        subtitleContext: ActivitySignature,
        config: CorrelationConfig,
    ): CorrelationResult
}

sealed interface SpeechProbeResult {
    data class Success(
        val signature: ActivitySignature,
        val actualStartMs: Long,
        val actualDurationMs: Long,
    ) : SpeechProbeResult

    data object Unsupported : SpeechProbeResult
    data object ResourceDenied : SpeechProbeResult
    data object Cancelled : SpeechProbeResult
    data class Failure(val reason: String) : SpeechProbeResult
}

interface SpeechProbeSource {
    suspend fun probe(
        mediaUri: String,
        targetPositionMs: Long,
        durationMs: Long,
        bucketMs: Int,
    ): SpeechProbeResult
}

interface SubtitleSyncRepository {
    suspend fun get(

        subtitleFingerprint: String,
        subtitleLanguage: String?,
        model: SubtitleSyncModel,
        confidence: Float,
        engineVersion: Int,
    )

package com.watermelon.app.migration

import com.watermelon.app.BuildConfig

/**
 * Compile-time migration flags for the Kotlin-to-Rust cutover.
 *
 * All flags default to false in CI and release builds. They can only be enabled for a local
 * debug build with a Gradle property, which keeps the migration reversible without adding a
 * user-facing setting or a network-controlled switch.
 */
internal object MigrationFlags {
    val useRustCore: Boolean get() = BuildConfig.USE_RUST_CORE
    val shadowMode: Boolean get() = BuildConfig.RUST_SHADOW_MODE
    val debugLogging: Boolean get() = BuildConfig.DEBUG && BuildConfig.RUST_DEBUG_LOGGING

    val environment: String
        get() = if (BuildConfig.DEBUG) "debug" else "release"
}
EOF
cat > app/src/main/kotlin/com/watermelon/app/migration/RustMigrationLog.kt <<'EOF'
package com.watermelon.app.migration

import android.util.Log

/**
 * Local-only comparison logging for shadow mode (D-4). No telemetry, upload or non-debug
 * logging is performed. Calls are no-ops unless the local opt-in BuildConfig flag is set.
 */
internal object RustMigrationLog {
    private const val TAG = "RustMigration"

    fun compare(component: String, kotlinValue: Any?, rustValue: Any?) {
        if (!MigrationFlags.debugLogging) return
        Log.d(TAG, "$component kotlin=$kotlinValue rust=$rustValue")
    }

    fun unavailable(component: String, reason: String) {
        if (!MigrationFlags.debugLogging) return
        Log.d(TAG, "$component rust unavailable: $reason")
    }
}
EOF

# Foreign-language bindings

By now you have setup your crate and `cargo build` has successfully created your library.

The next step is to have UniFFI generate source code for your foreign language. It doesn't help you build this code, it just generates it for you.

## Creating the bindgen binary

First, make sure you have installed all the [prerequisites](./Prerequisites.md).

Ideally you would then run the `uniffi-bindgen` binary from the `uniffi` crate to generate your bindings,
but if not on [Cargo nightly](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/unstable.html#artifact-dependencies),
you need to create a binary in your project that does the same thing.

Add the following to your `Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[[bin]]
# This can be whatever name makes sense for your project, but the rest of this tutorial assumes uniffi-bindgen.
name = "uniffi-bindgen"
path = "uniffi-bindgen.rs"
```

Create `uniffi-bindgen.rs`:
```rust
fn main() {
    uniffi::uniffi_bindgen_main()
}
```

You can now run `uniffi-bindgen` from your project using `cargo run --features=uniffi/cli --bin uniffi-bindgen [args]`

### Multi-crate workspaces

In a multiple crates workspace, you can create a separate crate for running `uniffi-bindgen`:

  - Name the crate `uniffi-bindgen`, add it to your workspace.
  - Add this dependency to `Cargo.toml`: `uniffi = {version = "0.XX.0", features = ["cli"] }`
  - As above, add the `uniffi-bindgen` binary target

Then your can run `uniffi-bindgen` from any crate in your project using `cargo run -p uniffi-bindgen [args]`

## Running uniffi-bindgen using a library file

Use `generate --library` to generate foreign bindings by using a cdylib file built for your library.
This can be more convenient than specifying the UDL file -- especially when multiple UniFFI-ed crates are built together in one library.
This should be used where possible - some "external type" features don't work otherwise.

In our example, we generate the bindings with:
```
cargo build --release
cargo run --bin uniffi-bindgen generate --library target/release/libmath.so --language kotlin --out-dir out
```
(maybe `.dylib`, good luck with `.dll`!)

Then look in the `out` directory.

When using library mode, if multiple crates get built into the library that use UniFFI, all will have bindings generated for them.

Library mode comes with some extra requirements:

  - It must be run from within the cargo workspace of your project
  - Each crate must use exactly 1 UDL file when compiling the Rust library.  However, crates can have
    multiple UDL files as long as they ensure only one is used for any particular build,
    e.g. by using feature flags.
  - Rust sources must use `uniffi::include_scaffolding!` to include the scaffolding code.

## Running uniffi-bindgen with a single UDL file

As noted above, library mode is encouraged - building from a single UDL is not recommended.

Use the `generate` command to generate bindings by specifying a UDL file.

### Kotlin

From the example directory, run:
```
cargo run --bin uniffi-bindgen generate src/math.udl --language kotlin
```
then have a look at `src/uniffi/math/math.kt`

### Swift

Run
```
cargo run --bin uniffi-bindgen generate src/math.udl --language swift
```
then check out `src/math.swift`

Note that these commands could be integrated as part of your gradle/Xcode build process.

This is it, you have an MVP integration of UniFFI in your project.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Audit and finish the Kotlin-to-Rust migration in Watermelon MediaPlayer after the repository owner approved all proposals.
- Complete Stages 3–6 (Rust port, binding, parity, cutover, cleanup) with all execution evidence from GitHub Actions.

## Requirements
- No local tests or local toolchain installation; all builds/tests/benchmarks via GitHub Actions.
- Local checks only: YAML parse, `git diff --check`, `sha256sum -c`.
- Keep unrelated pre-existing `Docs/` → `docs/` changes excluded from all commits.
- Owner decisions must be explicit; proposals are not approvals unless the owner says so.
- User wording: “Approve all proposals (Recommended)” and “finish the migration”.

## Decisions
- Owner approved D-1–D-6 on `2026-11-23`, recorded in `docs/migration/decision-log.md`.
- D-1: Continue past G0, conditional on G0 being met first.
- D-2: UniFFI, time-boxed spike; measure `SpeechLikelihoodAccumulator` ByteBuffer copy cost before committing to all twelve ports.
- D-3: 1e-6 tolerance for derived floats; bit-exact integers/Long/hash outputs; raw IEEE-754 bits diagnostic only.
- D-4: Local-only, opt-in debug logging of Kotlin vs Rust outputs; no telemetry/upload.
- D-5: Keep pure-Java MP3 encoder in `media-tools`.
- D-6: Approve one implementation owner + one independent reviewer before Stage 3 review; names still not supplied.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verify that all interfaces in common-interfaces have corresponding implementations."""

import os, re, sys

INTERFACES_DIR = "common-interfaces/src/main/kotlin/com/watermelon/common/repository"
CONTROLLER_DIR = "common-interfaces/src/main/kotlin/com/watermelon/common/controller"
IMPL_DIRS = ["library-storage", "subtitle-engine", "playback-engine"]

def find_interfaces():
    interfaces = {}
    for d in [INTERFACES_DIR, CONTROLLER_DIR]:
        for f in os.listdir(d):
            if f.endswith(".kt"):
                name = f.replace(".kt", "")
                interfaces[name] = os.path.join(d, f)
    return interfaces

def find_implementations():
    impls = set()
    for d in IMPL_DIRS:
        for root, _, files in os.walk(d):
            for f in files:
                if f.endswith("Impl.kt") or f.endswith("ControllerImpl.kt"):
                    impls.add(f.replace(".kt", "").replace("Impl", ""))
    return impls

def main():
    interfaces = find_interfaces()
    impls = find_implementations()
    missing = set(interfaces.keys()) - impls
    if missing:
        print(f"MISSING IMPLEMENTATIONS: {missing}")
        sys.exit(1)
    print("All interfaces have implementations.")
    sys.exit(0)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

- name: Upload spike artifacts

  android-ndk:
    name: Cross-compile UniFFI library with the Android NDK
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Set up Rust stable
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@df2a88e9fe4098bad09cb42c3dec7187f15861fc # stable
        with:
          toolchain: stable
          targets: aarch64-linux-android,armv7-linux-androideabi

      - name: Set up Android SDK and NDK
        uses: android-actions/setup-android@be39fa834029ff78f1a44aa3bb0819b8fc2bd8fd # v4.0.4
        with:
          packages: ndk;27.2.12479018 platform-tools

      - name: Generate lockfile
        working-directory: rust
        run: cargo generate-lockfile

      - name: Record NDK toolchain metadata
        run: |
          mkdir -p migration-ndk
          {
            echo "captured_at_utc=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
            echo "git_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            echo "workflow_run=${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"
            echo "rust_version=$(rustc --version)"
            echo "ndk_home=${ANDROID_NDK_HOME:-${ANDROID_NDK_ROOT:-unset}}"
            echo "ndk_version=$(grep '^Pkg.Revision' "${ANDROID_NDK_HOME:-${ANDROID_NDK_ROOT}}/source.properties" 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
          } > migration-ndk/metadata.txt
          cat migration-ndk/metadata.txt

      - name: Build arm64 and armv7 shared libraries
        working-directory: rust
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ndk_home="${ANDROID_NDK_HOME:-$ANDROID_NDK_ROOT}"
          toolchain=$(find "$ndk_home/toolchains/llvm" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d | head -1)
          test -x "$toolchain/bin/llvm-ar"

          export CC_aarch64_linux_android="$toolchain/bin/aarch64-linux-android24-clang"
          export AR_aarch64_linux_android="$toolchain/bin/llvm-ar"
          export CARGO_TARGET_AARCH64_LINUX_ANDROID_LINKER="$CC_aarch64_linux_android"
          cargo build -p watermelon-ffi --target aarch64-linux-android --release --locked

          export CC_armv7_linux_androideabi="$toolchain/bin/armv7a-linux-androideabi24-clang"
          export AR_armv7_linux_androideabi="$toolchain/bin/llvm-ar"
          export CARGO_TARGET_ARMV7_LINUX_ANDROIDEABI_LINKER="$CC_armv7_linux_androideabi"
          cargo build -p watermelon-ffi --target armv7-linux-androideabi --release --locked

      - name: Verify Android library ABIs
        working-directory: rust
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for target in aarch64-linux-android armv7-linux-androideabi; do
            library="target/$target/release/libwatermelon_ffi.so"
            test -s "$library"
            file "$library" | tee "../migration-ndk/$target-file.txt"
            grep -qi 'ELF' "../migration-ndk/$target-file.txt"
          done

      - name: Upload Android libraries
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: migration-ndk-libraries
          path: |
            migration-ndk/
            rust/target/aarch64-linux-android/release/libwatermelon_ffi.so
            rust/target/armv7-linux-androideabi/release/libwatermelon_ffi.so
          if-no-files-found: warn

- name: Build arm64 and armv7 shared libraries
        working-directory: rust
        run: |
          set +e
          {
            set -euo pipefail
            ndk_home="${ANDROID_NDK_HOME:-$ANDROID_NDK_ROOT}"
            toolchain="$ndk_home/toolchains/llvm/prebuilt/linux-x86_64"
            test -x "$toolchain/bin/llvm-ar"
            echo "toolchain=$toolchain"
            ls "$toolchain/bin" | grep -E '^(aarch64-linux-android24-clang|armv7a-linux-androideabi24-clang|llvm-ar)$'

            export CC_aarch64_linux_android="$toolchain/bin/aarch64-linux-android24-clang"
            export AR_aarch64_linux_android="$toolchain/bin/llvm-ar"
            export CARGO_TARGET_AARCH64_LINUX_ANDROID_LINKER="$CC_aarch64_linux_android"
            cargo build -p watermelon-ffi --target aarch64-linux-android --release --locked

            export AR_armv7_linux_androideabi="$toolchain/bin/llvm-ar"
            export CARGO_TARGET_ARMV7_LINUX_ANDROIDEABI_LINKER="$CC_armv7_linux_androideabi"
            cargo build -p watermelon-ffi --target armv7-linux-androideabi --release --locked
          } > ../migration-ndk/build.log 2>&1
          status=$?
          set -e
          cat ../migration-ndk/build.log

# Proposed decisions for owner approval

**Status:** Approved by the repository owner on 2026-11-23. D-1 through D-6 are now recorded in
`docs/migration/decision-log.md`, which remains the only authoritative decision record. This file
is retained as the rationale for those decisions, not as a second decision log.

Prepared 2026-11-23 from [migration-process-audit.md](migration-process-audit.md).

## D-1 — Continue past G0?

**Proposal:** Continue, conditional on G0 actually being met first.

**Rationale:** G0 currently has no golden corpus and no benchmark measurements, so "continue"
cannot be evaluated on evidence. The recommendation is to continue only after the generator,
ten JSON files, self-check, two-run checksum proof and at least one recorded benchmark run exist.
A stop decision remains legitimate if the measured JVM/device difference does not justify the
FFI and maintenance cost.

**Consequence if accepted:** Stage 3 may start only after the G0 exit criteria in [PLAN.md](PLAN.md).

## D-2 — Binding tool

**Proposal:** UniFFI, with a time-boxed spike before committing to all twelve ports.

**Rationale:** UniFFI generates both sides of the boundary and keeps the type contract in one
place, which matters for the many `FloatArray` and sealed-result types in the sync contracts.
Hand-written JNI gives more control over PCM buffer copying but is easier to get subtly wrong.
The spike must measure both correctness and the copy cost at the `SpeechLikelihoodAccumulator`
`ByteBuffer` boundary; if that cost dominates, revisit this choice.

**Consequence if accepted:** Add Rust toolchain and UniFFI generation to CI in Stage 3; no JNI
code until the spike reports.

## D-3 — Float tolerance

**Proposal:** 1e-6 tolerance for derived floating-point values, bit-exact comparison for integer,
Long and hash outputs.

**Rationale:** Kotlin/JVM and Rust/libm can differ in the last bits of `ln`, `roundToLong` and
other math used by `SubtitleProbeSelectorImpl` and `OffsetConsensus`. Raw IEEE-754 bits are
recorded in every golden vector, so a stricter rule can be adopted later without regenerating
anything. Bit-exactness across JVM and Rust for transcendental functions is not a realistic
acceptance rule on Android devices.

**Consequence if accepted:** Parity checker applies 1e-6 to decimal float results and exact
equality to bits of integer/hash results; raw bits remain diagnostic evidence, not pass/fail.

## D-4 — Shadow-mode logging policy

**Proposal:** Local only — opt-in debug logging of Kotlin vs Rust outputs, no telemetry, no upload.

**Rationale:** The app is commercial and its network surface is deliberately limited to subtitle
lookups. A shadow mode is needed for safe cutover, but it must not create a new data path.

**Consequence if accepted:** Add a debug-only flag in the app composition root and document a
rollback trigger before the first port.

## D-5 — MP3 encoder

**Proposal:** Keep the pure-Java encoder in `media-tools`.

**Rationale:** It is already validated in CI and has no NDK/JNI dependency. It is not one of the
twelve port candidates, and moving it would add risk without addressing the migration goal.

## D-6 — Migration owner and reviewer

**Proposal:** Owner to name one implementation owner and one independent reviewer before Stage 3.

**Rationale:** The audit found a PARTIAL stage merged with no recorded review. A named reviewer
is the simplest control for the decision-heavy stages ahead.

# Stage 3 report: Rust core, UniFFI spike and JVM parity

**Branch:** `migration/golden-oracle-scaffolding` · **PR:** #73
**Stage:** 3 of 6 · **Status:** IMPLEMENTED, GATE G1 NOT CLOSED

## Summary

The ten frozen Kotlin golden-vector components have Rust implementations under `rust/crates/core`,
and the D-3 comparator in `rust/crates/core/src/bin/parity.rs` passes all 39 committed cases.
A UniFFI boundary crate (`rust/crates/ffi`) and a workspace bindgen binary were added for the D-2
spike, with CI-generated Kotlin bindings. The D-2 PCM copy-cost measurement was executed on a
named GitHub-hosted runner. The Android NDK cross-compile job is in the same workflow.

No local Rust, Gradle or Android toolchain was installed or used. All execution evidence below is
from GitHub Actions. Stage 3 review cannot be signed off because D-6 names are still missing and
no on-device ART comparison has been performed.

## Evidence

| Item | Evidence | Result |
|---|---|---|
| D-1, D-2, D-3 approvals | [decision-log.md](decision-log.md) | Approved 2026-11-23 by SMozaff |
| Rust workspace compiles, tests and all targets | `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --locked` in workflow `migration-rust-parity.yml`; runs `45078413395`, `45078549135`, `45079298267`, `45079683879` | Green on the latest commit `f2375fb`; `cargo_exit=0` |
| Frozen-oracle parity, D-3 rule | `parity-report.txt` artifact from runs `45078549135`, `45079298267`, `45079683879` | `Rust parity: 39 cases, 0 failures`; 39 `PASS` lines; 1e-6 for derived floats, exact int/Long/hash, raw bits diagnostic |
| UniFFI Kotlin bindings generated from the built shared library | Workflow `migration-uniffi-spike.yml`, run `45079293229`; artifact `migration-uniffi-spike/build/uniffi-kotlin/uniffi/watermelon_ffi/watermelon_ffi.kt` | Generated successfully with UniFFI 0.29 in `--library` mode |
| D-2 PCM copy-cost spike | Same workflow, artifact `migration-uniffi/pcm-copy-report.txt`, run `45079293229` | 256,000-byte buffer, 3 warmup + 20 timed samples per path |
| Android NDK toolchain | `migration-uniffi-spike.yml` job `android-ndk`, NDK 27.2.12479018, arm64 + armv7 release libraries | Evidence to be recorded after the job's final green run |
| Golden oracle / JVM baseline prerequisites | Runs `45074382455` / `45075503837` | 10 files, 39 cases, 111,890 bytes, byte-identical; 7 workloads × 20 raw samples |

## D-2 spike result

The spike compares a borrowed PCM byte slice with an owned `Vec<u8>` copy (the boundary UniFFI
uses for Kotlin `ByteArray`) around the same parity-tested accumulator. Host metadata for run
`45079293229`: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, `rustc 1.100.0`, Intel Xeon 6975P-C, 4 vCPU, kernel
`6.14.0-1016-aws`.

| Path | Median ns | Mean ns |
|---|---:|---:|
| Borrowed `&[u8]` | 11,137,226 | 11,138,672 |
| Owned `Vec<u8>` copy | 10,986,942 | 10,988,803 |

The owned-copy path was slightly *faster* in this host measurement; the difference is well inside
sample noise and gives no evidence that PCM copying dominates the boundary. This supports
continuing with the approved UniFFI choice. These are host numbers, not ART/device numbers, and
are not a performance acceptance criterion.

## Defects found and fixed during Stage 3

1. **False-green CI (critical).** The parity step used `cargo run ... | tee ...`, so the pipeline
   exit status came from `tee` and run `45078413395` reported success while the report contained
   216 speech mismatches. Fixed with `set -o pipefail`; the corrected run `45078549135` genuinely
   failed or passed according to the comparator. No parity claim is based on the false-green run.
2. **Rust compile errors** from moving borrowed golden fields and a `parse_float(&Map)` type
   mismatch; fixed and re-verified in CI.
3. **Speech accumulator normalization** used `n` rather than Kotlin's `max(1L, n - 1L)` for
   `diffRms`/`zcr`; fixed and confirmed by the 39-case parity report.
4. **UniFFI bindgen CLI syntax.** UniFFI 0.29 requires `generate --library <path>`; the earlier
   positional form failed with `UDL file does not appear to be inside a crate`. The bindgen
   step now logs its output to an artifact on failure.

## Open before G1 / Stage 4 review

- D-6 implementation owner and independent reviewer names must be recorded in
  [decision-log.md](decision-log.md).
- One Rust function must be compared with Kotlin on an Android device using the D-3 rule; the ART
  protocol, device model and acceptance threshold have not been supplied by the owner. Host JVM
  parity is not a substitute.
- The UniFFI `.so` is built and generated Kotlin bindings are compiled in CI, but JNA, APK
  packaging and a native bridge are **not** part of this stage. No production call path calls
  Rust yet.

## Related documents

- [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) · [Decision log](decision-log.md) · [Stage 2 report](stage-2-report.md)
- [Kotlin signature inventory](kotlin-signatures.md) · [Migration process audit](migration-process-audit.md)

## Cutover and rollback design (scaffolding, not activated)

The app composition root now has three compile-time flags in `app/build.gradle.kts`, all defaulting
to `false`: `watermelon.useRustCore`, `watermelon.rustShadowMode` and
`watermelon.rustDebugLogging`. `MigrationFlags`, `RustMigrationLog`, `RustBridge` and
`MigrationDiagnostics` provide the D-4 seam. `AppDependencies.migrationDiagnostics` is deliberately
wired to `UnavailableRustBridge`, so no production path calls Rust and no APK change is implied.

Rollback triggers to apply before any flag is enabled in a non-local build:

1. Any non-numeric mismatch under the D-3 tolerance, or any integer/Long/hash mismatch, in the
   39-case JVM corpus → revert to the Kotlin implementation and stop.
2. Any mismatch on the owner-approved on-device protocol → revert and record the device, media
   and raw outputs before changing code.
3. A native-library load failure, missing ABI, or exception from the bridge → revert; shadow mode
   must never turn into a user-visible crash.
4. Any new telemetry, upload or non-debug logging → revert; D-4 permits local opt-in logging only.
5. A new dependency (for example JNA for UniFFI-generated Kotlin) or APK packaging change must be
   reviewed and approved before Stage 5; it is not covered by D-1–D-6.

## What this branch does

Completes the executable evidence that was missing from the Stage 2 audit, without starting the Rust port.

- **Fixes two suspected Kotlin defects before freezing the oracle** (per owner direction):
  - `BidiFormatter.format` now emits trailing neutrals after the PDI instead of inside the isolate.
  - `OpenSubtitlesHasher` now requires 131,072 bytes, matching the published OSHash reference.
  - Both are recorded in `docs/migration/defect-fixes.md` with regression tests.
- **Adds direct boundary tests** for the candidates that had none: probe selector, time mapper, drift corrector, sync config and `isRtl`.
- **Adds the Kotlin behavior oracle**: generator tests, structural self-checks, and an opt-in `workflow_dispatch` workflow. Ten JSON files (39 cases, 111,890 bytes) are committed under `testdata/golden/` with `SHA256SUMS` and provenance. No vector was hand-written.
- **Records the JVM baseline** that Stage 1 left unmeasured: an opt-in workflow ran the gated harness on a named `ubuntu-latest` runner; seven workloads × 20 raw nanosecond samples and host/JVM metadata are committed under `docs/migration/benchmark-results/`.
- **Adds `docs/migration/PLAN.md`** and reconciles the gate reports with dated post-audit sections that preserve the original historical records.

1. `docs/migration/decision-log.md` is unchanged: **D-1 through D-6 are still blank**. Proposals are only in `docs/migration/proposed-decisions.md` and must not be read as approvals. No Rust port has started.

## What this branch does

This branch now carries two related pieces of work.

### 1. Stage 2 evidence (original purpose)

Completes the executable evidence that was missing from the Stage 2 audit, without inventing results.

- Fixes two suspected Kotlin defects before freezing the oracle (per owner direction):
  `BidiFormatter.format` trailing-neutral placement and `OpenSubtitlesHasher`'s 131,072-byte minimum.
  Both are recorded in `docs/migration/defect-fixes.md` with regression tests.
- Adds direct boundary tests for probe selector, time mapper, drift corrector, sync config and `isRtl`.
- Adds the Kotlin behavior oracle: generator tests, structural self-checks and an opt-in
  `workflow_dispatch` workflow. Ten JSON files (39 cases, 111,890 bytes) are committed under
  `testdata/golden/` with `SHA256SUMS` and provenance. No vector was hand-written.
- Records the JVM baseline with seven workloads × 20 raw nanosecond samples and host/JVM metadata
  under `docs/migration/benchmark-results/`.
- Adds `docs/migration/PLAN.md` and reconciles the gate reports with dated post-audit sections.

### 2. Stage 3 Rust port and D-2 spike (added after owner approval)

- Ports all ten golden-vector components to `rust/crates/core` with a D-3 comparator that reads
  the frozen corpus. Parity is 39/39 with `set -o pipefail`, so the CLI's status cannot be masked by `tee`.
- Adds a UniFFI boundary crate and a bindgen binary; CI generates Kotlin bindings from the built
  `.so` and cross-compiles arm64/armv7 Android libraries with the NDK.
- Measures borrowed versus owned-copy PCM cost at the `SpeechLikelihoodAccumulator` boundary.
  The owned copy was not slower in the host run; copy cost does not justify abandoning UniFFI.
- Adds compile-time, default-false migration flags and a local-only D-4 shadow-mode seam. No
  production call path calls Rust and no APK/packaging change is included.

## CI evidence

| Evidence | Run |
|---|---|
| Golden oracle: two byte-identical generations and both self-checks | [`45074382455`](https://github.com/SMozaff/Watermelon-MediaPlayer/actions/runs/45074382455) — passed |

| UniFFI Kotlin binding generation and PCM copy-cost spike | [`45079891144`](https://github.com/SMozaff/Watermelon-MediaPlayer/actions/runs/45079891144) — passed |
| Android NDK arm64 + armv7 release libraries | [`45079891144`](https://github.com/SMozaff/Watermelon-MediaPlayer/actions/runs/45079891144) — passed |

`docs/migration/stage-3-report.md` records exact commands, artifacts and measured values. No tests
were run locally and no toolchains were installed.

## Owner decisions and remaining inputs

D-1 through D-6 are recorded as approved on 2026-11-23 in `docs/migration/decision-log.md`; the old
PR text saying they were blank is superseded. Still open:

1. D-6 names: one implementation owner and one independent reviewer. Stage 3 review cannot be signed off until they are recorded.
2. Confirmation of the reconstructed golden-vector JSON schema in `docs/migration/PLAN.md`.
3. Official `breakdance.avi` media through an approved test-data channel, if the published OSHash vector must be executable; the copyrighted asset is deliberately not committed.
4. On-device ART protocol, device model and acceptance threshold. Host JVM parity is not a substitute, so G1 remains open.
5. Approval before adding JNA/APK packaging or any production cutover; D-1–D-6 do not cover that dependency change.

package com.watermelon.app.migration

import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4
import com.watermelon.subtitle.bidi.BidiFormatter
import com.watermelon.subtitle.parser.SrtParser
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Test
import org.junit.runner.RunWith
import uniffi.watermelon_ffi.uniffiEnsureInitialized

/**
 * G1 device evidence: the Rust core runs on Android ART and is compared to the Kotlin oracle
 * with the D-3 rule (exact strings for these components). This test is built with
 * `-Pwatermelon.useRustCore=true -Pwatermelon.rustShadowMode=true
 * -Pwatermelon.rustDebugLogging=true` by migration-device-parity.yml.
 */
@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4::class)
class RustDeviceParityTest {

    @Test
    fun native_library_loads_on_art() {
        uniffiEnsureInitialized()
        assertTrue(MigrationFlags.useRustCore)
        assertTrue(MigrationFlags.shadowMode)
    }

    @Test
    fun bidi_functions_match_kotlin() {
        val samples = listOf(
            "hello world",
            "سلام دنیا",
            "mixed english و فارسی end",
            "abc (xyz) 123",
        )
        samples.forEach { text ->
            val rtl = BidiFormatter.isRtl(text)
            assertEquals("isRtl: $text", rtl, RustCutover.isRtl(text))
            assertEquals("format: $text", BidiFormatter.format(text, rtl), RustCutover.format(text, rtl))
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun srt_parse_matches_kotlin() {
        val srt = """
            1
            00:00:01,000 --> 00:00:02,500
            hello world

            2
            00:00:03,250 --> 00:00:05,000
            سلام دنیا
            second line (end)
        """.trimIndent()
        val expected = SrtParser.parseKotlin(srt, "fa")
        val actual = RustCutover.parse(srt, "fa")
        assertEquals(expected, actual)
        assertEquals(2, actual.cues.size)
    }
}
